blogs.title: Decoding Acute Neuro‑Behçet’s Disease When Imaging Is Silent
blogs.description: A deep dive into why neuro‑Behçet’s can appear at first presentation despite the classic several‑year lag, how normal brain MRI may mislead clinicians, and which clinical clues—headache pattern, aseptic meningitis CSF profile, mucocutaneous lesions—should trigger an early neuro‑BD diagnosis. Includes a practical algorithm for distinguishing acute neuro‑BD from infectious meningoencephalitis.

blogs.title: When the Brain Calls for Water: Unmasking SIADH in Neuro‑Inflammatory States
blogs.description: Reviews the diagnostic criteria for SIADH and explains how CNS inflammation—including acute neuro‑Behçet’s—drives inappropriate ADH release via cytokines such as IL‑6. Provides a stepwise approach to identify true SIADH among other hyponatraemia etiologies in patients with fever, headache and euvolemic status, and highlights key laboratory thresholds.

blogs.title: Colchicine Takes Center Stage: Rethinking First‑Line Therapy for Acute Neuro‑Behçet’s
blogs.description: Challenges the dogma that high‑dose corticosteroids are obligatory for acute neuro‑BD by examining evidence from this case where colchicine monotherapy resolved both mucocutaneous and neurological manifestations plus SIADH. Discusses colchicine’s anti‐neutrophil and cytokine‐suppressive actions, weighs its efficacy against steroids/immunosuppressants, and outlines patient scenarios where a steroid‑sparing strategy may be preferable.

blogs.title: The Silent Danger of Hyponatraemia: Hiccups, Rhabdomyolysis and the Art of Safe Sodium Correction
blogs.description: Highlights underappreciated complications of profound hyponatraemia—persistent hiccups as a red flag and rhabdomyolysis reflected by striking CK elevations. Explains the pathophysiology linking cellular swelling to muscle injury, outlines monitoring recommendations (serial CK, electrolytes), and provides evidence‐based sodium repletion protocols to avoid rapid overcorrection and osmotic demyelination.

blogs.title: From Rash to Fever: A Pragmatic Algorithm for ED Evaluation of Suspected Behçet’s with CNS Symptoms
blogs.description: Presents an emergency‐department focused decision tree when patients arrive with oral/genital ulcers or folliculitis‑like rash plus fever/headache/hyponatraemia. Emphasizes using the International Criteria for Behçet’s Disease over broad autoantibody panels, judicious ordering of ACE/sIL‑2R tests, targeted imaging/CSF analysis, and early specialty consultation to streamline diagnosis while avoiding low‐yield investigations.
